new_value: Perplexity CEO publicly committed to a 2028 IPO target (June 9, 2026), holding the line regardless of rival Anthropic/OpenAI filings; CBO casts it as deliberate discipline to build a healthy, high-growth business.
headline: Perplexity sets a concrete 2028 IPO target, a self-imposed marker of financial discipline
so_what: Reload the 'is Perplexity stable enough to bet on against a trillion-dollar Google?' objection: the rep can now cite a public, self-imposed pre-IPO timeline to reframe Perplexity as a disciplined growth company.

new_value: Perplexity shipped Brain, a self-improving agent memory (Research Preview, Max/Enterprise Max), claiming 25% higher accuracy, 16% better recall, and 13% lower cost on repeat tasks.
headline: Perplexity ships Brain, a self-improving memory layer for its Computer agent
so_what: Gives reps a concrete, shipped talking point in the contested agentic race against Google's Search Agents: an agent that learns from its own runs overnight and traces each memory to a source. Use it as momentum, not proof. The gains are first-party and it is Research Preview on the $200 Max tier only.

new_value: John Jumper (AlphaFold Nobel laureate) leaving DeepMind for Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer leaving for OpenAI, two exits in 48 hours, Alphabet down more than 5%.
headline: Google DeepMind loses its Nobel laureate and a Gemini co-lead to Anthropic and OpenAI in one week
so_what: When Google leans on its full-stack 'we own the models and the research' moat, reps can answer that DeepMind's bench is being poached by the very rivals Perplexity orchestrates (Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT). It reframes Google's research edge as eroding rather than fixed.

new_value: Gemini 3.5 Pro missed Pichai's I/O 'next month' (June) target and is reportedly delayed to July, roughly four months after the prior frontier release (Gemini 3.1 Pro in February).
headline: Gemini 3.5 Pro slips past Pichai's June launch promise to a reported July
so_what: Gives reps a concrete CEO timeline miss to counter Google's 'we ship fast, full-stack' pitch, and it pairs with the DeepMind departures to argue Google's model cadence is slowing. It does not change what reps concede about Gemini 3's current benchmark standing.

old_value: DeepMind Nobel laureate John Jumper announced June 19 he is leaving Google for Anthropic (one high-profile defection).
new_value: Four senior Google AI researchers exited inside a fortnight: Noam Shazeer to OpenAI, then John Jumper, Jonas Adler, and Alexander Pritzel to Anthropic. The pull cited is compute access and pre-IPO equity at the rivals.
headline: Google's DeepMind exodus widens to four senior researchers in a fortnight, three bound for Anthropic
so_what: When a buyer frames Google's in-house AI as the safe long-term standard, the rep now has a concrete counter: four senior people from the Gemini and AlphaFold core left in two weeks, three to Anthropic, with the reasons being TPU queues and equity at rivals. That turns 'Gemini is the durable default' into 'Gemini's bench is thinning,' which strengthens the case for a model-neutral layer that routes to best-of-breed instead of betting the stack on one vendor whose top researchers are walking out.

new_value: July 1, 2026: a Stockholm court ordered Google to pay ~$1.97B to Klarna's PriceRunner, the largest competition damages award in Swedish history, for self-preferencing its shopping service. Google is weighing an appeal.
headline: Swedish court hits Google with record $1.97B antitrust damages over Shopping self-preferencing
so_what: Gives reps a concrete number for the neutrality pitch: a court just put a roughly $2B price on Google steering users to its own service, so 'Google favors itself over the fair answer' stops being an abstraction and becomes a verdict you can cite next to the DOJ and EU cases.

new_value: EU binding decisions due July 27, 2026 will force Google to open Android system-level AI access (wake word, screen context, on-device hardware) to rivals and share Search data with AI chatbot providers. A July 8 General Court ruling removed Google's pre-emptive challenge.
headline: EU locks in July 27 orders forcing Google to open Android's AI layer to rivals
so_what: Reps can answer the 'Google is too embedded on Android to displace' objection with a date: in the EU, rival AI providers (Perplexity included) are on track to get the same wake-word, on-screen and hardware access Gemini has today, so Google's mobile default status is a shrinking, legally contested advantage rather than a permanent moat.

headline: Strengthened the Comet security objection rebuttal: reps can now name SPACE, Perplexity's per-session sandbox that isolates every Computer task in its own VM and keeps credentials out of the sandbox.

old_value: Gemini 3.5 Pro slipped to July 2026 per I/O guidance (Pichai said the model would arrive 'next month').
new_value: Months behind schedule with coding short of internal expectations; Alphabet shares fell 4% on the Bloomberg report (July 16, 2026).
headline: Gemini 3.5 Pro is now months late, weak on coding, and Alphabet's stock dropped 4%
so_what: When a buyer says Google owns the best models so a neutral layer is redundant, reps can point out Google's flagship is months late and short on coding while OpenAI and Meta ship, which is the case for picking the best model per task rather than one vendor's roadmap.

old_value: European Commission finalizing its largest-ever DMA fine, a 'high triple-digit million euro' penalty for ranking its own Shopping, Flights and other services above rivals (amount unspecified, not yet issued)
new_value: €890M ($1B) fine issued July 23, 2026: €460M for search self-preferencing plus €430M for Play Store anti-steering, with 60 days to comply or face penalties up to 5% of worldwide turnover. Google is weighing an appeal.
headline: EU issues Google its first DMA fine: €890M and a 60-day order to stop self-preferencing in Search
so_what: Hardens Perplexity's neutrality pitch against the 'Google is too embedded to displace' objection: a rep can now cite a concrete first-ever EU fine and a 60-day order forcing Google to stop ranking its own shopping and travel results above rivals in Search, the same self-serving mechanism Perplexity's cited, ad-free answers avoid. The €890M is trivial against Alphabet's $109.9B quarterly revenue and is under appeal, so it is a talking point that reinforces an existing narrative, not a deal-flipping event on its own.

new_value: On July 16, 2026 the EU ordered Google to license its anonymised Search query, click, ranking and view data to rival search engines and, explicitly, to AI chatbots that offer search, on FRAND cost-recovery pricing, with sharing due to begin January 2027 for eligible EU providers.
headline: EU orders Google to hand its Search query and click data to rival search engines and AI answer chatbots, starting January 2027
so_what: Blunts the 'Google's search-data scale is an unmatchable moat' objection in EU deals. From January 2027 an eligible EU search provider, and AI chatbots that offer search, can license the same anonymised query, click and ranking data Google uses to tune its own results, so a rep can argue regulators are prying the moat open rather than conceding it is permanent. Hold it as watch, not act: sharing has not started, it is EU-only, and Perplexity's eligibility under the EU-search-engine thresholds is unconfirmed.

new_value: UK Competition Appeal Tribunal certified an opt-out class action (~880,000 advertisers, up to £5B / $6.7B) over Google's alleged search-ad overcharging, cleared to trial (Aug 5, 2026).
headline: UK tribunal clears a £5B advertiser class action against Google to proceed to trial
so_what: Hands reps a fresh, concrete UK overhang for the 'Google is too embedded to displace' objection: a court just let 880,000 businesses pursue Google for up to £5B over the same search-ad dominance a buyer would be standardizing on. It reinforces the neutrality wedge but sets no liability and moves no price or product, so it is ammunition to cite, not a reason to change the live pitch yet.

headline: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash three weeks after 3.6 and halves the price
so_what: Drop the 'Google is stalling on models' talking point: its Flash workhorse is shipping every three weeks and just cut API price in half. Concede the benchmark and price fight, win on neutrality and citations.

new_value: From September 4, 2026 every Android Assistant user is force-migrated to Gemini across phones, tablets, watches, earbuds and Android Auto, with no opt-out and no rollback.
headline: Google force-migrates every Android phone from Assistant to Gemini on Sept 4
so_what: Reps can no longer frame Google's AI reach as something users opt into. Every Android Assistant user becomes a Gemini user automatically, so concede the distribution point up front and lead with what a forced default can't give: ad-free, cited answers and the freedom to route across models.

new_value: Google took a $12.2B warrant option in Marvell to co-develop custom TPU-ecosystem chips, adding a second silicon partner alongside Broadcom.
headline: Google deepens its custom-silicon stack with a $12.2B Marvell chip warrant
so_what: Google is buying deeper into owning its whole AI stack from the chips up, so a Perplexity rep should not try to win on infrastructure scale. Push the neutrality wedge instead: Google routes you to its own Gemini running on its own silicon, while Perplexity lets you pick the best model for each task and switch vendors.
